title: The Clever Carpenter's Measure (ES)
summary: A carpenter builds an enormous royal carriage inside a courtyard with a narrow gate. Birbal solves the dilemma without knocking down the palace walls. [ES]
full_text:
The master carpenter of the imperial carriage works was commissioned to build a grand ceremonial chariot of teak and gold for Emperor Akbar's coronation anniversary. The carpenter worked for six months inside an inner walled courtyard of the royal workshops.

When the magnificent chariot was finished—towering twelve cubits high, with carved ivory wheels and gold-plated canopy—the carpenter prepared to roll it out to the parade ground.

To his absolute horror, he realized that the stone archway of the courtyard gate was only nine cubits high and ten cubits wide! The colossal chariot was completely trapped inside the courtyard!

The master carpenter threw himself on the ground in panic. The royal engineer advised knocking down the historic marble archway, but Akbar was furious: 'That archway was built by my grandfather! You cannot demolish historic palace masonry to rescue a carriage!'

Birbal arrived to inspect the trapped chariot. 'Sire, the archway need not be touched, nor the carriage dismantled.'

Birbal asked the royal laborers to bring shovels and picks. 'Dig two smooth, deep trenches into the dirt road beneath the archway, exactly where the chariot's wheels must pass, lowering the ground level by three cubits. Lay wooden planks along the trenches.'

The laborers dug the trenches within three hours. The giant chariot rolled down into the trenches, lowering its overall height so that its golden canopy cleared the stone archway with ease, rolling out onto the parade ground without a scratch!

Once the chariot passed, the laborers filled the trenches and repaved the road.

Akbar cheered: 'Brilliant, Birbal! When the ceiling is fixed, a wise man simply lowers the floor!' Akbar rewarded Birbal and the carpenter, celebrating the power of creative perspective.
